0.0.n: Used to acknowledge or introduce the next topic.

0.2.n: Points to something near the speaker and directly modifies the title that follows.

0.4.n: This is the title of the game being discussed.

0.6.n: A polite ending identifying the game.

0.7.n: Invites the listener to share recognition of the game.

0.9.n: Introduces the speaker as the topic; the usual は is omitted in casual speech.

0.11.n: 版 means edition or version, attached here to 英語.

0.12.n: Past form of 出る, used here for a game's release.

0.13.n: 出た時 means the time when it was released.

0.14.n: Marks the release as the starting point of the speaker's interest.

0.15.n: Emphasizes that the speaker's interest was fairly strong.

0.16.n: Part of 気になる, an expression for something catching your interest or occupying your thoughts.

0.17.n: Links 気 to なる within 気になる; it is not translated separately in natural English.

0.18.n: なっていて is なる + ている in a connecting form, showing continuing interest and leading into the next clause.

1.0.n: The first part of the company name Fantasy Flight.

1.1.n: The second part of the company name Fantasy Flight.

1.2.n: さん can follow company names to sound respectful or friendly, not just people's names.

1.3.n: Connects the company name to 方 in a softened expression for the source.

1.4.n: 方 means side here; の方から softens the reference to the company as the source.

1.5.n: Marks the company as the source of the planned import.

1.6.n: The connecting て-form of 輸入する links importing the game with playing it.

1.7.n: Combines with する to describe playing a game.

1.8.n: The intention form of する; with かな, it presents an action the speaker is considering.

1.9.n: Works with な to express a question the speaker asks themself.

1.10.n: Completes かな, giving the proposed action a tentative, self-questioning tone.

1.11.n: Marks the preceding idea as the content of the speaker's thought.

1.12.n: Past plain form of 思う, describing an earlier consideration.

1.13.n: Short for の; with です, it presents the thought as background information.

1.14.n: Makes the explanation polite; the past tense is already expressed by 思った.

1.15.n: Introduces a contrast with the earlier plan; も makes this a slightly fuller version of けど.

2.0.n: 版 identifies this as the Japanese-language version of the game.

2.1.n: Marks 日本語版 as what came out.

2.2.n: Past form of 出る, referring to publication or release.

2.3.n: A conversational substitute for と in ということ, introducing the information about the release.

2.4.n: Packages the preceding statement as a situation to consider.

2.5.n: This is the でし portion of でしたら, not a standalone word.

2.6.n: Completes でしたら, the polite conditional form of です: if that is the case.

2.7.n: Adds a conversational appeal to the listener after the condition.

3.0.n: Names the version the speaker wants to use for playing.

3.1.n: Marks the edition used to play, rather than the location of play.

3.2.n: Expresses strong enthusiasm for doing the desired action.

3.3.n: Pairs with したい to express wanting to play the game.

3.4.n: する becomes したい to express the speaker's desire.

3.5.n: Marks プレイしたい as the content of the speaker's thought.

3.6.n: Polite past form of 思う, describing the decision or feeling that motivated the purchase.

3.7.n: Connects the speaker's desire to its result by giving a reason.

3.9.n: Shows that the speaker acted promptly after deciding.

3.10.n: 入手する + てみる adds a trying-it-out nuance; ました makes the ending polite and past.

0.lit: Yes, this Witcher, right. I, since the English edition came out, have been quite interested, and…
0.tip: 気になる means something catches your interest; 気になっていて shows that interest continuing.

1.lit: From Fantasy Flight's side, importing and perhaps playing, I thought, but…
1.tip: しようかなと思った means the speaker was considering doing something, rather than firmly planning it.

2.lit: If it is the case that the Japanese edition came out, you see…
2.tip: ってことでしたら means if that is the case, treating the reported release as a basis for the next decision.

3.lit: Using the Japanese edition, I thought I definitely wanted to play, so I promptly tried obtaining it.
3.tip: てみました means actually doing something to try it out, not making an unsuccessful attempt.
